brief.headline: Add a think/act/prove gate before agents open a PR
brief.summary:
Three separate repos landed on the same fix for the thing that actually breaks unattended runs: agents that call work done when it isn't. fable-method and fivetaku/fablize both formalize a think/act/prove loop with an eval or evidence check before the agent stops, and ponytail's lazy-senior-dev persona attacks the same problem from the other end by cutting scope creep. Pair either with cobusgreyling/loop-engineering's loop-audit to see what your existing overnight loop is actually doing before you trust it further.

On cost, opencodex now proxies Codex CLI and Claude Code to any backend including local Ollama, and kimi-k3-in-c runs a 2.78T-parameter model on a single CPU in 8GB RAM — worth benchmarking as a free tier for low-stakes subagent calls, alongside the unverified but concrete TielCoder 22GB quant claim. claude-code-router 3.0.22 fixes SSE corruption and forwards prompt_cache_key on openai_responses, a real cache-hit improvement if you route through it. For working away from the desk, devspace and CopilotKit/OpenBot give you phone-triggerable or sandboxed action-logged sessions. And before your next six-hour unattended run, note the new research on inference engines themselves being an exploitable attack surface, not just the sandbox around them.
bullets: Install fivetaku/fablize as a Claude Code plugin to force Opus through a completion/evidence/verification procedure before it opens a PR
Run loop-audit from cobusgreyling/loop-engineering against your current overnight agent loop to see what it does and costs
Route low-stakes subagent calls through lidge-jun/opencodex to a local Ollama model, or bench kimi-k3-in-c / the 22GB TielCoder quant as a free CPU tier
Upgrade claude-code-router to v3.0.22 for the prompt_cache_key fix on openai_responses, and pull Claude Code v2.1.243 for its 33 fixes
Try Waishnav/devspace or CopilotKit/OpenBot to trigger or steer an agent from your phone with a reviewable action log
Re-check what host access your inference engine (vLLM, llama.cpp, Ollama) has — it's now a documented attack surface for unattended runs

signals.label: Prove-before-ship verification loops
signals.note: fable-method, fablize, and ponytail independently converge on forcing evidence/verification before an agent calls a task done

signals.label: Frontier-class coding on commodity hardware
signals.note: kimi-k3-in-c (CPU-only, 8GB RAM) and a 22GB TielCoder quant both claim to compete with paid tiers on real coding work

signals.label: Away-from-desk agent control
signals.note: devspace, omnigent, and OpenBot all ship phone- or remote-triggerable sessions with logged actions this cycle

signals.note: researchers now flag the inference engine itself, not just sandboxing around tool calls, as exploitable

items.title: lidge-jun/opencodex — Universal provider proxy for OpenAI Codex & Claude Code — use any LLM (Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Ollama…) with Codex CLI, App, SDK, and Claude Code
items.tldr: opencodex is an open-source proxy that lets Codex CLI/App/SDK and Claude Code call any LLM backend, including local Ollama models.
items.whyItMatters: You can route cheap or local models into your existing Claude Code workflow instead of paying frontier prices for every subagent call.
items.tryThis: Clone lidge-jun/opencodex and point a low-stakes subagent at a local Ollama model through it.

items.title: cobusgreyling/loop-engineering — Practical patterns, starters & CLI tools for loop engineering with AI coding agents. Design systems that prompt and orchestrate agents (inspired by Addy Osmani and Boris Cherny). Includes loop-audit, loop-in
items.tldr: loop-engineering ships CLI tools (loop-audit, loop-init, loop-cost) for designing and auditing agent prompt loops.
items.whyItMatters: loop-audit and loop-cost give you a concrete way to check what an unattended agent loop is doing and costing before you let it run overnight.
items.tryThis: Clone cobusgreyling/loop-engineering and run `loop-audit` against one of your existing agent loops.

items.title: FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c — A 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 running inference on a single CPU in 8.24 GB of RAM. Portable C99: no BLAS, no framework, no GPU.
items.tldr: kimi-k3-in-c runs the 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 model on a single CPU in 8.24GB of RAM using portable C99, no GPU, BLAS, or framework required.
items.whyItMatters: A trillion-parameter-class model now runs on ordinary CPU hardware you already own, useful for routing low-stakes work off paid APIs.
items.tryThis: Clone FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c and benchmark it on a spare machine as a free tier for low-stakes subagent tasks.

items.title: NanoNets/Graft — Turbocharge Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini & every coding agent: faster, cheaper, with contextual understanding specific to your codebase.
items.tldr: Graft adds codebase-specific context indexing to speed up and cut token costs for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini agents.
items.whyItMatters: Less redundant context per call means cheaper, faster runs across the tools you already use.
items.tryThis: Install NanoNets/Graft on your mobile app repo and compare token usage on a task you'd normally hand to a subagent.

items.title: Waishnav/devspace — Turn ChatGPT into Codex! OR Turn Claude Web into Claude Code!
items.tldr: devspace turns the ChatGPT or Claude web chat interface into a Codex- or Claude-Code-like coding agent session.
items.whyItMatters: Lets you trigger or steer a coding agent from your phone's browser, closer to a describe-and-walk-away workflow.
items.tryThis: Try Waishnav/devspace from your phone browser to kick off a coding task while away from your desk.

items.title: CopilotKit/OpenBot — Open-source AI coworkers that each get a computer of their own: a browser, files and tools, with every action decided before it happens and recorded after. Bring any AG-UI agent.
items.tldr: CopilotKit ships OpenBot, an open-source harness that gives each agent its own sandboxed computer with pre-action approval gates and a full action log.
items.whyItMatters: Gives you a concrete pattern for letting an agent run unattended while still producing an auditable trail you can review in the morning instead of a black box.
items.tryThis: Clone CopilotKit/OpenBot and wire an AG-UI agent to it for a sandboxed, action-logged run.

items.title: Sahir619/fable-method — The Fable Workflow: how Claude Fable 5 worked, distilled into skills any model can run, with the eval that keeps it honest. Think / act / prove.
items.tldr: fable-method distills the workflow behind Claude Fable 5 into portable skills plus an eval, structured as think / act / prove.
items.whyItMatters: Gives you a concrete verification-loop pattern to make a subagent prove its work before it opens a PR.
items.tryThis: Drop the fable-method skills into your Claude Code skills folder and wire its 'prove' step into your PR-review hook.

items.title: Gitlawb/zero — The coding agent that answers to you, your model, your machine, your rules.
items.tldr: Gitlawb/zero is a self-hosted coding agent written in Go that lets you plug in your own model and run it on your own machine.
items.whyItMatters: A concrete path to route routine coding-agent work to a self-hosted or local model instead of paying per-token for a hosted one.
items.tryThis: Clone Gitlawb/zero and point it at a local model to compare cost and output quality against your current setup on routine tasks.

items.title: eneskirca/nodeterm — Node-based terminal manager for AI coding agents — tmux-backed terminals and parallel agent sessions as draggable nodes on an infinite pan/zoom canvas. macOS, Linux, and a browser Server Edition.
items.tldr: nodeterm is a tmux-backed terminal manager that lays out parallel AI-agent sessions as draggable nodes on an infinite pan/zoom canvas, for macOS, Linux, and browser.
items.whyItMatters: Built for exactly the multi-worktree, multi-subagent setup you already run; could replace manual tmux/terminal juggling.
items.tryThis: Clone eneskirca/nodeterm and try it against your current worktree and subagent session layout tonight.

items.title: fivetaku/fablize — A Claude Code plugin that makes Opus behave like Fable — completion, evidence, and verification enforced as procedure. Ships only what a Fable-vs-Opus comparison proved transferable.
items.tldr: fablize is a Claude Code plugin that forces Opus through a completion/evidence/verification procedure modeled on Fable, shipping only what a Fable-vs-Opus comparison proved transferable.
items.whyItMatters: Adds a concrete verification gate to Opus runs so it self-checks evidence before finishing, closer to a PR you can trust unattended.
items.tryThis: Install fivetaku/fablize as a Claude Code plugin and route overnight Opus tasks through its verification procedure.

items.title: Show HN: Kern – container and resource runtime in a 1.5 MB binary, no daemon
items.tldr: Kern is a 1.5MB, no-daemon Rust binary that runs OCI containers with cgroup v2 resource limits, starting boxes in about 3.5ms.
items.whyItMatters: A daemonless, near-instant sandbox is a lighter way to cage agent shell commands than spinning up Docker for every task.
items.tryThis: Swap Docker for kern when sandboxing agent-run commands that only need CPU/RAM limits, not a full container runtime.

items.title: v3.0.22
items.tldr: Claude Code Router 3.0.22 fixes SSE multi-byte corruption and oversized JSON preview crashes, and now forwards session id as prompt_cache_key on openai_responses.
items.whyItMatters: The prompt_cache_key forwarding improves cache hit rates on OpenAI-compatible routes, and the SSE fix stops corrupted streamed output mid-run.
items.tryThis: Upgrade claude-code-router to v3.0.22 now if you route any traffic through openai_responses.

items.title: llm-anthropic 0.27
items.tldr: llm-anthropic 0.27 adds compatibility with the new anthropic v1.0.0 Python SDK, which switches from httpx to httpx2, mirroring an OpenAI SDK change two weeks earlier.
items.whyItMatters: If you pin anthropic<1 or run the llm CLI against Claude, this is a breaking dependency change you need to handle before it bites you.
items.tryThis: Run `pip install -U llm-anthropic 'anthropic>=1'`; if you maintain your own integration, point an agent at anthropic's MIGRATION.md and have it upgrade and fix tests, the way Willison did.

items.title: TielCoder's 22 GB 4-bit quant matches Opus4.6 medium on recent real life coding issues, surpassing KAT-Coder and Nail as strongest and fastest MoE picks.
items.tldr: A 22GB 4-bit GGUF quant of a 35B-A3B MoE coder, TielCoder, reportedly matches Opus 4.6 medium on real coding issues while running fast on constrained hardware.
items.whyItMatters: A concrete local-model candidate for offloading routine coding subagent work from paid API calls, pending your own verification of the single-poster benchmark.
items.tryThis: Download the TielCoder GGUF and run it as your cheap-tier coding subagent for a week of real tasks.

items.title: DietrichGebert/ponytail — Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. The best code is the code you never wrote.
items.tldr: Ponytail is a prompt/persona repo that pushes coding agents to write the least code possible, like a lazy senior dev.
items.whyItMatters: A minimal-code persona can cut scope creep and rework on unattended runs, which matters when nobody reviews until morning.
items.tryThis: Pull ponytail's system prompt into your agent's default instructions and test it on one overnight task before wider rollout.

items.title: omnigent-ai/omnigent — Omnigent is an open-source AI agent framework and meta-harness: orchestrate Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, and custom agents — swap harnesses without rewriting, enforce policies and sandboxing, and collaborate in rea
items.tldr: Omnigent is an open-source meta-harness that orchestrates Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and other agents under one policy and sandboxing layer, controllable from any device.
items.whyItMatters: Gives you one place to enforce guardrails across agents you run unattended, and a way to check in from your phone instead of your desk.
items.tryThis: Try omnigent-ai/omnigent as a policy layer in front of your Claude Code worktree setup and test its remote-device control path.

items.title: oomol-lab/open-connector — Open-source auth gateway connecting 1000+ SaaS providers to AI agents through SDK, CLI, MCP, HTTP, and OpenAPI.
items.tldr: Open-connector is an open-source auth gateway that links agents to over 1000 SaaS providers via MCP, SDK, CLI, and HTTP.
items.whyItMatters: It gives your agents one auth layer for SaaS tools instead of custom OAuth code for each service you connect.
items.tryThis: Clone oomol-lab/open-connector and wire it as an MCP server for the SaaS tools your agents need.

items.title: fuxicodex/Fuxi — FuXi is a fast, self-contained AI coding agent that lives in your terminal — edit code, run commands, and drive tools, with cost-aware routing across LLM providers.
items.tldr: Fuxi is a terminal coding agent with built-in cost-aware routing across multiple LLM providers.
items.whyItMatters: It's a candidate harness if you want provider routing built in instead of writing your own tiering logic.
items.tryThis: Try Fuxi on a small repo task and compare its provider-routing behavior to your current router setup.

items.title: larlarua/AutoCVE — Agent-driven automated CVE discovery platform for source code auditing, vulnerability verification, and report generation.
items.tldr: AutoCVE is an open-source agent pipeline that audits source code, verifies vulnerabilities, and generates CVE reports automatically.
items.whyItMatters: A ready-made subagent for security scanning you can bolt onto a pre-merge hook instead of building one yourself.
items.tryThis: Clone larlarua/AutoCVE and run it against a repo as a pre-merge security-audit subagent.

items.title: OCR It – pull text out of un-copyable documents for your LLM
items.tldr: OCR It is a tool that pulls text out of un-copyable documents so you can feed them to an LLM.
items.whyItMatters: Turns screenshots, scanned specs, or locked PDFs into text an agent can actually use as context.
items.tryThis: Run OCR It on a design doc or scanned spec before pasting it into an agent prompt.

items.title: Claude Code v2.1.243
items.tldr: Claude Code v2.1.243 shipped 60 changes: 10 added, 12 improved, 33 fixed, 5 changed.
items.whyItMatters: This is a substantial update to the exact tool you run every night, worth checking before your next unattended session.
items.tryThis: Update to v2.1.243 and skim the changelog for anything touching hooks, subagents, or worktrees.

items.title: v1.18.22
items.tldr: OpenCode 1.18.22 fixes device login links, guards textVerbosity for OpenAI-compatible providers, and patches the Bedrock provider.
items.whyItMatters: If any subagent routes through OpenAI-compatible or Bedrock providers in OpenCode, this update removes a live error path.
items.tryThis: Update OpenCode to v1.18.22 if you use OpenAI-compatible or Bedrock providers.

items.title: Advancing price-performance for developers with GPT‑5.6 in Kiro
items.tldr: GPT-5.6 is now available inside Kiro, AWS's agentic IDE, with improved price-performance for planning, building, reviewing, and testing code.
items.whyItMatters: If you use Kiro for any of your agent work, this is a cheaper or faster model tier to route work to without changing your setup.
items.tryThis: If you use Kiro, switch a build/review task to GPT-5.6 and compare cost and output against your current model.

items.title: not much happened today
items.tldr: Persistent/self-modifying agent harnesses Headlong and exo add rollback and continuous-operation features, and Anthropic ships MCP connectors with managed auth for long-running workloads.
items.whyItMatters: Rollback and continuous operation are exactly what unattended overnight agent runs need to recover from bad state without you watching.
items.tryThis: Check the Headlong and exo repos for a rollback mechanism you can bolt onto your worktree-based overnight runs.

items.title: Quoting Drew Breunig
items.tldr: Drew Breunig says Fable's high cost ended the habit of waiting for a cheaper model to fix your bill, forcing explicit decisions about which work goes to which model tier.
items.whyItMatters: Backs deliberately routing routine subagent work to cheaper models instead of defaulting everything to your top-tier model.
items.tryThis: Audit your subagent config and move routine tasks (lint, test runs) off your top-tier model onto a cheaper one.

items.title: deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness — DeepSeek Harness: Everything is a Plugin.
items.tldr: DeepSeek open-sourced deepseek-harness, an agent harness built entirely around a plugin architecture.
items.whyItMatters: Worth a look as a possible plugin-based supplement to your Claude Code setup, though the listing gives no specifics on what plugins ship yet.
items.tryThis: Clone deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness and check whether its plugin API covers anything your hooks/skills setup doesn't.

items.title: LLMs could control their host machines by exploiting inference engines
items.tldr: Security researchers describe how LLMs could exploit vulnerabilities in inference-serving engines to gain control of the host machine.
items.whyItMatters: If you leave agents running unattended overnight, the inference engine itself is an attack surface, not just the sandbox around its tool calls.
items.tryThis: Re-check what host-level access your inference engine (vLLM, llama.cpp, Ollama) has before an unattended overnight run.

clusters.summary: A proxy and two model options make it concrete to shift subagent work off paid frontier APIs.

clusters.title: Control agents away from the desk
clusters.summary: Phone-web bridges and sandboxed, action-logged harnesses for steering or auditing agents outside your normal terminal session.
